items: Ten million businesses at ~1 KB each is about 10 GB, small enough for one Postgres instance.
Two-dimensional "near me" queries need a geospatial index (PostGIS, geohash), not two B-tree indexes.
Keep the average rating correct under concurrent reviews by updating it atomically in the same transaction.

blocks.text: Naive: WHERE lat BETWEEN … AND lng BETWEEN …. Two 1-D B-tree indexes can't do a 2-D range efficiently.

items: Add a geospatial index (PostGIS GiST, ST_DWithin) and pg_trgm for name search. 10GB fits one Postgres, so no extra search cluster yet.
~20k searches/sec: serve reads from replicas and cache hot business pages in Redis. The primary only takes writes.
Reviews: a unique (user, business) constraint, and the average updated in the same transaction as the insert, with no lost updates.
Which geo index?
Geohash: prefix = area, B-tree friendly; query the cell plus 8 neighbours to handle edges. Quadtree: adapts to density.
Average rating with concurrent reviews?
Store sum and count; UPDATE … SET sum=sum+:r, count=count+1 in the review's transaction. That is an atomic operation, so no lost update.
One review per user?
A DB unique constraint, not an application check (check-then-insert races).
When would you add Elasticsearch?
Only if search needs relevance ranking, fuzzy matching, and facets beyond pg_trgm, or QPS outgrows replicas.
A geo-sharded cluster for 10GB of data. One Postgres with PostGIS plus replicas is enough.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
